subject: Unexpected September usage — token origin & VAT treatment
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@touchstone.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected September usage spike — help?

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing a ~4.6x jump in token consumption on our September invoices compared to our August baseline. Our procurement team is holding payment while we reconcile the delta — the line item points to 'conversation/generation' tokens but we have not changed our integration. Can you: 1) confirm whether any model or tokenization changes on Redwood's side could cause reclassification, and 2) provide a per-request sample (timestamps, model, input token count, output token count) for the largest 3 days in the spike window (Sep 6–8)?

Also — because Touchstone is an EU-registered subsidiary billing through our US entity, we need clarity on VAT treatment for any retroactive credits (reverse-charge vs refund). The invoices team copied here (invoices@touchstone.ai).

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Finance — Touchstone AI
elena@touchstone.ai

Attachment: invoice-20260901-touchstone.pdf
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected September usage spike — help?

Elena — thanks for the quick note and for attaching the invoice. We’re looking into it. Initial answers up front:

- No intentional pricing change on our side. There was a model rollout in early September for one of the variants in your account's routing policy (an updated decoder with slightly different tokenization heuristics) — that can surface as higher "input" tokens in some edge cases.
- We can provide per-request samples and the aggregated day-level breakdown for Sep 1–10; attaching a snapshot extract (token-usage-snapshot-20260921.csv).
- On VAT: we will coordinate with Kimberly in our billing team to confirm whether a credit should be processed as a vendor credit (refund) or as a reverse-charge adjustment.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll run a quick reconciliation and flag the subset of requests routed to the new decoder variant.
2) Ben will scope whether this is a measurement/tokenization delta (we then propose a one-off pro-rated credit) vs duplicated ingestion (which would be a full credit).
3) Kimberly will confirm VAT/legal handling and timing.

We’ll aim to get back with a proposal by end of day Sep 23. If that timing is tight for your AR team, let me know and we can prioritize.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0192

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected September usage spike — quick internal notes

Tessa / Kim — quick internal read:
- Causes to consider in order: (1) routing to the new decoder variant with denser tokenization, (2) a change in client-side batching that increased per-request tokenization overhead, (3) rare duplicate replays from Touchstone's nightly job (we saw a small pattern last June).
- I'll run a per-model attribution query against request logs for Sep 1–10 and flag requests where model_variant != pinned_version. That should give us the population to propose a targeted credit.
- For an initial trust-preserving move, recommend offering a provisional credit equal to the delta for the spike days (Sep 6–8) pending deeper trace. Suggest 30% provisional credit on that delta while we confirm. Helps unblock AR.

I'll hand the attribution output to Tessa when ready.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@touchstone.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, invoices@touchstone.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected September usage spike — reconciliation & provisional credit

Hi Elena — following up with our reconciliation and next steps. Apologies for the longer note but wanted to be transparent.

Summary of findings (Sep 1–10 window):
- Total token delta vs Aug baseline: +4.6x; spike concentrated on Sep 6–8.
- Attribution: ~72% of the additional tokens were routed to a decoder_variant that rolled out to a small fraction of traffic on Sep 4 (we had a narrower rollout that expanded automatically because of rollout rules).
- Root cause: the variant uses a slightly different byte-pair tokenization boundary for certain punctuation-heavy prompts used by Touchstone's nightly summarization job. That increased input token counts for long, multi-paragraph inputs. No duplicate replays detected.

What we are proposing:
1) Provisional credit: Redwood will issue a provisional adjustment equal to 50% of the token delta for Sep 6–8 (calculated on the attached CSV). This will appear as a credit memo against invoice 20260901 within 3 business days once you confirm acceptance. (We selected 50% to fairly share the risk while we confirm there were no client-side batching changes.)
2) Full trace deliverables: we included a per-request log sample and a model-variant attribution csv in the Drive folder below; Ben will hand over the query results on Sep 24.
3) VAT treatment: Kimberly reviewed with billing/legal — because Touchstone invoices are issued to your US billing entity, we propose processing the adjustment as a vendor credit (refund/credit memo) on our US invoice. If you need this treated as a reverse-charge for EU VAT purposes, please confirm the receiving EU entity and provide the VAT ID and legal contact; we will escalate to our tax team.

Drive (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLink/usage-snapshots
Attached: token-usage-snapshot-20260921.csv (aggregated sample), provisional-credit-agreement.docx

Please confirm: 1) acceptance of the provisional 50% credit, and 2) if the adjustment needs reverse-charge handling (provide EU VAT ID if yes). Once we have confirmation, we’ll schedule the credit and share the credit memo/Docusign if needed.

Thanks — appreciate your patience and partnership.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
